candidates.explanation: This is the only code in the snippets that changes a user's provider to a non-email value. When a social login finds an existing user by email whose status is inactive, it overwrites user.provider and user.socialId with the social provider's values and saves them. A freshly registered email user is inactive until they confirm, so this branch hijacks the account. The user is then stuck with provider='google', and email login fails with needLoginViaProvider:google. Upstream, a user found by email is just used as-is and is never rewritten. I could not see the register and confirm-email code, so this is inferred from the snippets.

This is where the 422 needLoginViaProvider:<provider> is thrown. It fires because the stored user.provider is not 'email'. It reports the problem but is probably not the root cause: the provider value was set wrongly elsewhere, either in the social-login path or in the register or confirm-email path.

fix.description: In validateSocialLogin, remove the inactive-status block (lines 135-140) that overwrites user.provider and user.socialId and calls update. When a user is found by email, use that user as-is and do not change an email-registered user's provider. Also check the register and confirmEmail code to make sure they keep provider = AuthProvidersEnum.email.
